source: workflow wf_0ff6eac9-728: proposals per lens + grounding skeptic verdicts, verbatim

props.lens: detection power: which observed invariants separate honest from tampered/inconsistent logs most sharply, with the lowest measured honest false-positive rate and the smallest detectable deviation

proposals.name: Server-minted id bracket and binding test (provider request/response ids as a third clock bound to each response)
proposals.observation_summary: ids_and_clocks_in_ids/O5 (skeptic numbers): one constant client-server skew per stream places every server-id time between the stream's last input event and the response's first output block in all but 10 of 3,674 swechat streams (rate 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466]; tolerance 0 gives 18, 5 s gives 7); cc_local 1 of 847; aiv_cu Anthropic opus/sonnet/haiku/fable 105/80/27/32 and Gemini pro/flash 255/92 streams all 0; OpenAI 3/463. Skew-interval width U-L p5 1,102 / p50 2,268 / p95 3,807 ms. Placebo on 3,673 swechat streams: rolling the id sequence by one response flags 3,667; moving one response's first event 5 s earlier flags 1,441, 30 s earlier flags 3,581; moving it 5 s, 30 s or 300 s later flags 10, which equals the baseline. ids/O1: swechat request ids are v7|var2 in 154,815/154,815 against 2,418.98 expected by chance; cc_local 31,085/31,085. ids/O2: counting every copy, request-id time agrees with the client stamp in 155,067/155,267 = 0.99871 [0.99676, 0.99992]; holdout A 11,047 ids, 0 violations. ids/O6: a naive offset >= 0 rule fails on client skew (cc_local 125 violations in 3 sessions, min -7,749 ms) that the bracket absorbs. ids/O7: in 2 re-stamped session pairs the id clock picks the earlier copy in 178/178 (disagreeing offsets >= 619,473 ms vs agreeing 2,347-21,734 ms).
proposals.test_measurement: Extend the O5 placebo scripts (scratchpad rd/o5.py, o5b.py, o5c.py) into a tamper suite on swechat B Claude Code streams, holding the honest rate at 10/3,674 and reporting session-clustered CIs: (1) insert a fabricated tool_result before response k, stamped on a grid of offsets (0.5-60 s) before and after the request-id time; (2) splice a whole response with its request id from another session, or from later in the same session; (3) delete one response; (4) back-date one response on a 1-30 s grid (finer than the measured 5 s / 30 s points) to locate the displacement giving power 0.5 and 0.9, to be compared with U-L p50 2,268 ms; (5) collapse a block of entries onto one timestamp as in ids/O7. Replicate on holdout A (11,047 ids), cc_local (847 streams) and aiv_cu Anthropic (post-switch), Gemini and OpenAI streams. Report power per tamper type, not pooled.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: 10/3,674 swechat streams inconsistent at 2 s tolerance (18 at 0 s, 7 at 5 s); client clock skew behind the server (ids/O6: cc_local min -7,749 ms, split A -16,359 ms), which breaks per-event rules but leaves the bracket at 1/847; resume/fork copies with re-stamped history (ids/O7: 2 session pairs, 477 entries), which is why counting every copy lowers O2 agreement to 0.99871 with 190 offsets over 10 min; second-resolution ids (ids/O3: OpenAI and Gemini ids have 1 s resolution; aiv_cu OpenAI 3/463 inconsistent).
proposals.evasion_cost: The agent cannot see or predict the id: the provider mints it when the request arrives (ids/O2 mechanical explanation), so a model fabricating results in-band cannot produce a consistent one. A log editor can: the ids are unsigned base58/hex strings and anyone who knows the layout (itself UNVERIFIED against documentation, ids/O1) can mint a v7 id with a chosen time for an inserted or moved response. Late-stamping is invisible by construction (later shifts flag only the baseline 10), resolution is per turn rather than per event, and edits that leave timing alone (content substitution, status flips) are invisible.
proposals.coverage: Measured where server ids exist: swechat 155,267 (session, request) ids in 1,638 sessions forming 3,674 streams; cc_local 31,085 request ids, 847 streams; aiv_cu Anthropic only after the 2026-07-06 message-id switch (ids/O4: 0 UUIDv7 msg ids from 2025-04 to 2026-06), Gemini 255/92 and OpenAI 463 streams. aiv_cc has none (ids/O13: 0 request ids stored). Share of all tool results constrained: not measured; a stream needs at least 2 responses.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Time-in-identifier forensics (UUIDv1, ULID, Snowflake) is a known general technique. Using LLM-provider request ids as a per-stream skew bracket and a response-binding test on agent tool logs may not be described; we have not checked. It is neither a capture-side witness (the id already exists) nor a hash chain.
proposals.rank_reason: The only invariant with a measured tamper-power curve: misbinding is flagged in 3,667 of 3,673 streams and a 30 s back-date in 3,581, against an honest 10 of 3,674, using a value the agent cannot see.

proposals.name: Visible-text vs harness structured-copy recount at 1-unit resolution
proposals.observation_summary: raw_census/A6-O1 (skeptic, full population): Claude Code's harness Read counter toolUseResult.file.numLines equals the number of line-numbered lines in the model-visible result text in 87827/88229 = 0.9954, Wilson [0.9950, 0.9959], cluster [0.9947, 0.9960] over 4603 files. All 402 mismatches are named harness or dataset formats: 282 persisted-output previews, 105 'file shorter than offset' warnings, 7 '<identical to result [rN]...>' references, 7 redacted contents and 1 negative line numbers; none is unexplained. cc_local main 570/578, all 8 mismatches empty-file warnings with diff -1. raw_census/A6-O2: a subagent's totalToolUseCount equals its distinct nested tool_use ids in 6623/6623, Wilson [0.9994, 1.0], 1934 files. raw_census/A6-O4: the same structured copy also carries Edit structuredPatch line counts (70553/73460 = 0.960 filled) and Grep numLines (29535/34208 = 0.863); their agreement with the visible text was not measured.
proposals.test_measurement: Pre-register the whitelist from A6-O1 (persisted-output preview, offset warning, identical-to reference, REDACTED, negative line numbers; plus cc_local's empty-file warning) and re-run on the full swechat CC population and cc_local main; the expected honest unexplained count is 0. Tamper suite on a random sample of clean Read results: add or delete 1, 2 or 5 lines; splice in a same-path Read result from another session; substitute content with the line count held fixed. Report detection per tamper type; arithmetic predicts every line-count change is caught and no count-preserving substitution is, and the run should confirm both. Do the same for A6-O2 by deleting or inserting one nested tool_use in agent_progress traffic. Then measure agreement, not only presence, for Grep numLines vs result lines and for Edit structuredPatch oldLines/newLines vs the call's old_string/new_string line counts, and report their honest unexplained rates.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: the 402 swechat mismatches are all harness display formats or dataset redaction, and cc_local's 8 are empty-file warnings (diff -1); a detector without the whitelist would fire on every one. Not false positives but blind spots: 2150/8773 = 0.245 [0.236, 0.254] of Agent/Task results have no nested traffic and cannot be checked (A6-O2); cc_local subagent files carry no Read numLines (0 of 12); Glob totalMatches is absent in swechat (0/6422).
proposals.evasion_cost: Low for a schema-aware editor. Both fields are written by the same harness from the same read (A6-O1 and A6-O2 mechanical explanations: internal redundancy, not an independent witness), so rewriting numLines alongside the text evades the check, and line-count-preserving substitutions are invisible by construction. The model does not author toolUseResult, so a model writing a fake result into its own text produces no counter at all. The check therefore targets post-hoc edits made without schema knowledge and harness or export faults, not in-band claims.
proposals.coverage: Read results carrying numLines: 88229/90763 = 0.972 in swechat (A6-O4); cc_local main 578/650 = 0.889. Agent/Task results checkable: 6623 in 1934 files, with 2150/8773 uncheckable. Edit and Grep counters are present (0.960, 0.863) but their agreement is not yet measured.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Consistency between redundant fields is a generic data-integrity idea. Using Claude Code's toolUseResult structured copy as a cross-check on the model-visible result seems unexplored to us, but we have not checked. It differs from Tool Receipts (purpose-built, capture-side) because the field already exists, and it is neither recomputation of the command (METR) nor output grammar parsing (jc).
proposals.rank_reason: Among the lowest measured honest false-positive rates in the data, and the only one of them tied to result content (0 unexplained in 88229 Read results once 5 named formats are whitelisted; 6623/6623 subagent counts), at 1-line or 1-call resolution; ranked below rank 1 because both fields come from one writer.

proposals.name: Execution-window consistency: time evidence in or around a result must fit the window in which it was supposedly produced
proposals.observation_summary: Nearly every fresh clock reading or timer we checked that real execution leaves in or around a result fits that result's own call-to-result window, and most exceptions have a cause visible in the log (re-reads, display rounding, re-stamped blocks). commit_witness/O9 (skeptic): commit SHAs printed in Bash results resolve for 3936 claims in 1491 sessions, and commit_date lies in [call ts - 2 s, result ts + 2 s] for 3917 = 0.995 [0.992, 0.998], median offset -0.103 s. commit_witness/O11: of the 19 claims whose commit_date precedes the window, 15 are cat/tail/head/grep re-reads of earlier output files, 1 is an amend with an explicit GIT_COMMITTER_DATE and 3 are unexplained. ext_witness/O10: epochs printed with a fractional part (time.time() form) never postdate the external wiki save, 0/459 (Wilson upper 0.0083); without a fraction 7/123. two_clocks/O6: Codex's model-visible 'Wall time' header never exceeds the call-to-output gap for exec_command (0 violations in 4408 at 2 ms, min slack 153 ms), while 0.1 s-display shell_command headers exceed it in 646/1817 by <= 49 ms. two_clocks/O8: harness tool timers lie inside the window (swechat Glob 1/2090, WebFetch 0/341, WebSearch 0/158, Task 0/1023, Agent 0/1886), and two_clocks/O12 places that one Glob case on a timestamp shared by 180 entries. two_clocks/O9: bash_progress ticks obey the floor rule in 0/112677 violations (Wilson hi 3.41e-5, 687 sessions), result >= last tick 5676/5676, per-call phase residual range median 6 ms. Negative control ids_and_clocks_in_ids/O14: stored v7 uuids printed in results are not fresh (440 of 561 mentions more than 10 min older), so only freshly generated readings qualify.
proposals.test_measurement: On swechat CC B raw transcripts and Codex rollouts: (1) classify each result's printing command as generator or re-reader using a list fixed in advance from commit_witness/O11 (cat/tail/head/grep of a file, TaskOutput and background .output reads are re-readers); (2) extract fresh absolute readings (resolved git '[branch sha]' to commit_date; ISO datetimes and 10-digit epochs from generator commands) and printed durations (Codex 'Wall time', test-runner 'in X s', shell 'real'); (3) compute the honest violation rate per class with session-clustered CIs, with tolerance 2 s for absolute readings (from O9) and the printed resolution for durations (from O6); (4) for swechat sessions that emit bash_progress, measure the share of Bash calls with gap >= 3 s that carry at least one tick, and tick count vs gap (not yet measured); (5) tamper suite: replay a real clock-bearing output from earlier in the session or from another session for the same command, shift stamps by a grid of deltas, drop ticks; report power vs delta at the measured honest rate. Stop rule: if fresh readings occur in too few results to matter, report that share and stop.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: re-reads of saved output (15 of the 19 out-of-window commit claims, identifiable by command); explicit committer dates (1); 3 unexplained of 3936 resolved claims; display rounding (shell_command headers 646/1817, by <= 49 ms) and write_stdin poll stamps (14/1600, min -36.1 ms); bulk re-stamped blocks (two_clocks/O12; timing checks must abstain on tie runs); machine suspend (two_clocks/O10: 1 progress event over its timeout among 83521); stored ids and dates echoed by tools (ids/O14); auto-backgrounded commands whose result window is not the execution window (outliers/O9: 111 of 188 swechat 120 s shell results were auto-backgrounded); sandbox clock offset (ext_witness/O10 median -1 s). A SHA that does not resolve is not usable alone: 2198/6141 = 0.358 [0.321, 0.394] of honest commit claims do not resolve (commit_witness/O10).
proposals.evasion_cost: The agent sees neither the harness stamps nor future commit dates at second resolution, so it cannot print a consistent fresh reading without actually running a command. A log editor controls the stamps, so for plain date-style outputs and Wall time headers they can keep printed values and stamps in step once they know the rule. The git leg costs more: the commit date is hashed into the SHA and the commit lives in an external repo, so moving a commit claim in time, or inventing one, needs a real commit made at that time. Forging ticks needs a phase-locked 1 Hz chain whose first tick falls at elapsed 2 or 3 s.
proposals.coverage: Measured pieces only: resolved commit claims 3936 in 1491 sessions (out of 6141 claims in 1839 sessions); Codex exec_command Wall time headers 4408; bash_progress ticks on 5702 calls (687 sessions) in swechat, none in cc_local (raw_census/A6-O10: no progress entries); fraction-form epochs 459, in collusion-wiki only. Share of all tool results that carry a fresh clock or a printed duration: not measured.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Unlike METR-style recomputation of deterministic outputs (echo, wc), this bounds outputs that cannot be recomputed by the log's own clock. Timestamp-consistency auditing is generic, and the git leg overlaps our own git shadow-state plan.
proposals.rank_reason: Second-scale resolution with rare honest misses that the printing command mostly explains (19 of 3936 commit claims, 15 of them re-reads), partly anchored on a content-addressed external object; ranked third because the share of results carrying a fresh clock is unmeasured.

proposals.name: Quantized server-usage ledger of result modality (per-image and cache-block units)
proposals.observation_summary: token_conservation/TC9 (skeptic): in aiv_cu Gemini the per-window change in prompt IMAGE tokens is 0 or exactly one per-model unit in 11668 of 11668 pairs (258 for gemini-2.5-pro, n 4925; 1064 for 3-pro 682, 3.1-pro 3166 and 3.5-flash 2895), never negative. It is positive in 5059/5092 GUI windows and 0 in every non-GUI window: shell 0/4134, get_pixel_coords 0/2033, pause 0/202. distributions/D3: prompt-side image tokens sit on the per-model lattice in flash 3219/3219 and pro 10569/10569 ({258, 1064, 2160}), and no session mixes lattices (0/309). aiv_accounting/O11: in aiv_cc, where screenshots are stripped from the log, the context residual per image is tightly concentrated (pre-registered fit: median 890.1 [887.9-890.9], p25 879.1, p75 892.7, n=4543 pairs in 64 runs), above the honest per-turn |residual| p99 of 690.2 (aiv_accounting/O10). The level depends on the model: a no-intercept model gives 1112.5, and token_conservation/TC17 gives 1035.0 (p5-p95 1016-1142) for aiv_cc but 535.0 (p5-p95 121-1618) for user-pasted swechat images. swechat_tables/T11: Codex cached_input_tokens is a multiple of 128 in 16106/16106 calls.
proposals.test_measurement: aiv_cu Gemini (11945 pairs): predict IMAGE units per window from the logged action types and require dIMAGE = units x per-model constant; measured honest exceptions are 33/5092 GUI windows with no increment and 0 in non-GUI windows. Tamper suite: delete one GUI result, relabel a GUI action as shell, insert a fabricated screenshot-returning call and result, splice in a window from another session; report detection at the honest rate for each direction. Also test the regime above 40 images that the B sample never reached (442 population sessions with more than 40 GUI turns). aiv_cc: count [IMAGE_REMOVED] markers per window, test the residual against the per-image constant, and tamper by adding or removing one marker; report power at FPR 1% with run-clustered CIs, treated as a one-agent case study. Codex: cached_input_tokens % 128 == 0 as a plausibility check on fabricated usage rows.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: 33/5092 GUI windows show no increment (not cap effects; images before median 4, max 31); the unit depends on model generation (258, 1064, and 2160 in 70 rows from 3 sessions); cached IMAGE counts are off-lattice (11/3022 and 40/9318), so only prompt-side counts are checkable; aiv_cc has 30 unlogged context resets, 27 of them image pairs (aiv_accounting/O12); user-pasted images vary in size (swechat p5-p95 121-1618), so a per-image constant holds only for uniform screenshots; Claude cache tokens show no 128 granularity (1/563).
proposals.evasion_cost: The model never sees usage metadata. A log editor can rewrite it, since it is unsigned. Screenshots stay in context (up to 40 observed), so adding or removing one image shifts IMAGE and promptTokenCount for every later response in the session, and the editor must propagate the change consistently through all of them. Swapping one screenshot for another of the same unit, or editing text, is invisible to this ledger.
proposals.coverage: Exact ledger only in aiv_cu Gemini: 11945 pairs; two_clocks/O7 puts Gemini rows in 347 of 2000 B sessions. aiv_cc: 4543 single-image pairs in 64 runs of effectively one agent (token_conservation/TC2: all its sessions are runs of a single sdk_session_id). Codex 128 rule: 16106 calls. No per-modality breakdown was observed for Anthropic or OpenAI-chat usage.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Plausibility checks on token counts are familiar in billing. We have not seen the provider's per-modality token counts used as an exact ledger of how many image-returning results a log may contain, but we have not checked.
proposals.rank_reason: Exact, server-written integer witness at 1-image resolution with 0 honest increments across 4134 shell, 2033 get_pixel_coords and 202 pause windows; ranked fourth for narrow coverage (aiv_cu Gemini, plus one-agent aiv_cc).

proposals.name: Frozen usage-ledger reconciliation at tolerance 0 (commit-time tally and end-of-run result row)
proposals.observation_summary: swechat_tables/T1 (skeptic): a 5-integer token/API tally written by the Entire CLI at commit time equals, with tolerance 0, an exact recount of the stored transcript (distinct message.id, last-occurrence usage) over the whole transcript, a prefix or a contiguous window in 4794/4836 = 0.9913 [0.9883, 0.9936] Claude-format sessions (repo-clustered [0.9874, 0.9942], 183 repos). Prefix sessions are snapshots taken while the session continued: created_at precedes the last transcript timestamp in 1664/1664 prefix sessions, with a median of 3 messages past the snapshot. T2: the window class is explained by the declared checkpoint_transcript_start in 357/357. T3: after correcting a dataset join artifact, unmatched is 33/5701 = 0.0058 [0.0041, 0.0081] across 4 scaffolds; Claude format 4822/4836. T4: residual rate by CLI version 0.4.x 11/3691 = 0.0030, 0.5.x 15/1048 = 0.0143 [0.0087, 0.0235]. aiv_accounting/O7: in Agent SDK runs, result.usage is never above the sum of logged per-response usage (0 of 211 runs); the 15 runs below it are explained exactly by subset sums of responses with non-null stop_reason (12/12, plus 3 all-zero runs). aiv_accounting/O4: num_turns == user rows + 1 in 153/154 non-trivial runs.
proposals.test_measurement: On the swechat sessions with tallies (5701): run a tamper suite on honest sessions inside the snapshotted range. Delete one assistant message (all records of one message.id); insert a message.id copied from elsewhere; append messages after the snapshot point; insert a fabricated tool_use block into an existing message.id; edit result content. Report the detection rate per tamper against the honest unmatched rate 33/5701, overall and per CLI version. The recount rule predicts that 1-message deletions and insertions inside the snapshot are caught, while post-snapshot appends and block-level insertions into an existing message are not; the run should confirm both. Then couple the frozen usage with per-call token conservation and report the smallest content edit detectable once usage cannot be edited; the current per-call figure is swechat CC power 0.5/0.9 at 8913/10000 inserted chars, and 0.0099 at +3000 chars (token_conservation/TC2). Repeat on aiv_cc result rows (211 runs) by deleting or inserting a response with null stop_reason.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: 33/5701 unexplained after the join correction, higher in CLI 0.5.x (15/1048) and concentrated by repo (6 of 33 in hirakiuc/gh-orbit); 7 Claude residuals differ only in output_tokens (mid-stream snapshot, T4). The dataset join artifact (T3) must be corrected first, because it accounts for 31 of 64 raw mismatches. Checkpoint rows are duplicated across forks (T9: 3650/13406 rows), which double-counts in repo-clustered statistics. aiv_cc: 15/211 runs fall below the ledger, all explained by non-null stop_reason responses whose omission depends on SDK version and date (O7).
proposals.evasion_cost: The agent sees neither ledger. The Entire tally is written at commit time into the entire/checkpoints git branch (T9 mechanical explanation: forks copy that branch), so an editor must rewrite that branch as well; a rewrite is possible but is visible to anyone holding an older clone. Blind spots by construction: anything after the snapshot point; a tool_use block inserted into an existing message.id, since the recount keys on distinct message.id with last-occurrence usage; and any change to tool-result content, since usage does not change when a result is edited (T1 skeptic). Content edits then face only per-call token conservation, which misses edits under thousands of chars (TC2) and never catches deletion of results under 1k chars (TC16: [100,1000) power 0.003). The aiv_cc result row sits in the same log, so an editor can rewrite it together with the stream (aiv_accounting/O5: tokens and cost can be edited together).
proposals.coverage: swechat: tallies for 5701 sessions across 4 scaffolds (Claude format 4836 with api > 0), present only where the Entire CLI ran. aiv_cc: 211 runs of effectively one agent. Every assistant message before the snapshot point is constrained; tool-result content is not.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. The commit-time tally behaves like a seal, and sealing is prior art (Agent Flight Recorder, NovaFabric); ledger reconciliation is a standard audit idea. What may be new is that the seal already exists incidentally (Entire CLI) and freezes the provider usage that token conservation is then checked against.
proposals.rank_reason: Tolerance-0 equality at 1-API-message resolution with an honest unexplained rate of 33/5701 and an anchor stored outside the transcript, but blind to result content and to block-level insertion, so it constrains which turns exist rather than what results said.

ground.lens: detection power (grounding skeptic). All 5 proposals in analysis/out/phase_c/proposals_power.json were checked; the task text was cut off partway through rank 3. Every cited (lens, id) is in _index.json exactly once with reproduced == true, including raw_census/A6-O10, which is cited only in coverage text. Numbers were checked against the index's skeptic_numbers. The O5 placebo was also checked against the logic of scratchpad/rd/o5c.py.

checks.name: 1. Server-minted id bracket and binding test (provider request/response ids as a third clock bound to each response)
checks.overclaims: All quoted numbers match the skeptic values: O5 10/3,674, 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466], 18/7 at 0 s/5 s, widths 1,102/2,268/3,807, placebo 3,667, 1,441, 3,581 and 10; O2 155,067/155,267; O6 -7,749 and -16,359; O7 178/178. The overclaims are these. (1) The rank_reason says this is 'the only invariant with a measured tamper-power curve'. That is false: token_conservation/TC2 (reproduced) has a measured tamper-power curve (swechat CC D_abs inserted power 0.5/0.9 at 8913/10000 chars), and TC16 measures deletion power by result size. (2) 'Misbinding is flagged in 3,667 of 3,673' overreads the placebo. o5c.py cyclically rolls S across every response in the stream (np.roll), so every response is misbound at once and the last id's time lands on the first response. Power against splicing or swapping a single response is unmeasured; the proposal's own test 2 is what would measure it. The 'curve' is two back-date points, and they shift only the response's first-event t, not the input event before it. (3) The evasion text says 'a model fabricating results in-band cannot produce a consistent one'. This implies power the bracket does not have. The model never writes stamps or ids; the harness stamps a fabricating turn consistently, so in-band fabrication is invisible to the bracket. It only constrains post-hoc log edits that move, insert or misbind responses. (4) The ids/O7 result ('id clock picks the earlier copy 178/178') is implied by the offsets, per the skeptic, and is not independent evidence. The collapse onto 1-2 timestamps is detectable without any id clock. Honest resume/fork (O7) and old-harness blocks (two_clocks/O12) produce the same collapse, so tamper type 5 cannot be told apart from honest data. Rank 3 of the same set even says timing checks must abstain on tie runs. (5) The aiv_cu 'all 0' counts are cited without ids/O3's caveat that created_at row inserts lag the id by a median of 5.7-12 s, so the bracket there is weak by construction. Widths are reported only for swechat. (6) Minor: ids/O1's 154,815 silently includes 50 Vertex ids taken from api_msg_id, and 'constant skew within a session' (O6) rests on 1-2 sessions. The core claim still stands on reproduced O5: back-dating one response by 5 s or more is detectable against an honest 10/3,674, and late-stamping is not (acknowledged).
checks.prior_art_overlap_with_listed: Not a listed item directly. The closest listed entry is Gladyshev & Patel (2004 FSM reconstruction). The same authors' event-time-bounding work bounds an event's time between causally ordered, timestamped events with a clock-offset allowance; I recall it as IJDE 2005, unverified. That is essentially the bracket's logic, so any novelty claim should rest on using provider-minted request ids as the bound and the binding test, not on the bounding itself. The proposal already acknowledges time-in-identifier forensics (UUIDv1, ULID, Snowflake).

checks.name: 2. Visible-text vs harness structured-copy recount at 1-unit resolution
checks.overclaims: All quoted numbers match the skeptic values: 87827/88229 [0.9950, 0.9959], cluster [0.9947, 0.9960]; 402 = 282+105+7+7+1; cc_local 570/578; 6623/6623 [0.9994, 1.0]; 2150/8773; 70553/73460; 29535/34208; 88229/90763; 578/650; 0/6422; 0 of 12. The proposal handles the skeptic's mechanical explanation correctly: same writer, so internal redundancy. Remaining problems: (1) '0 unexplained once 5 formats are whitelisted' is in-sample. The whitelist was built after the fact from those same 402 mismatches, and the empty-file class from cc_local's 8. The test plan re-runs on the same swechat population and cc_local main, so 0 is guaranteed. The honest rate needs data the whitelist was not derived from, such as a holdout split or cc_local sessions after the analysis date. (2) The whitelist is itself an evasion route. Rewriting a result into a persisted-output preview, an offset warning or an identical-to reference exempts it, and the 402/88229 honest exemptions give cover. (3) Coverage for the A6-O2 leg is swechat-era only. raw_census/A6-O10, which the same author cites in rank 3, shows 0 progress/agent_progress entries in cc_local's 332 main and 840 subagent files. The subagent-count check therefore has no measured coverage on current Claude Code logs. (4) 'Tied to result content' means tied to the line count only; count-preserving substitution is invisible (acknowledged).
checks.prior_art_overlap_with_listed: None of the listed items. It is not METR recomputation, not jc grammar parsing, and not Tool Receipts, because the field already exists and is not purpose-built. Consistency between redundant fields is a generic integrity idea, as the proposal says.

checks.name: 3. Execution-window consistency: time evidence in or around a result must fit the window in which it was supposedly produced
checks.overclaims: All quoted numbers match the skeptic values: commit_witness/O9 3917/3936 in 1491 sessions, median -0.103 s; O11 19 = 15+1+3; O10 2198/6141; ext_witness/O10 0/459 and 7/123; two_clocks/O6 4408 and 646/1817; O8 1/2090 etc.; O9 0/112677 and 5676/5676; O10 1/83521; O12 180; ids/O14 440/561; outliers/O9 111/188. The skeptic corrections for O11 and outliers/O9 are applied. proposals.name: Provider-clock ceiling on each tool round: the interval between two server-minted request ids bounds every client-side duration claim for the call between them
proposals.observation_summary: Anthropic request ids decode as UUIDv7 (unix ms) in 154,815/154,815 swechat requests, against 2,418.98 expected by chance, and in 31,085/31,085 cc_local requests. The layout is inferred from data and is UNVERIFIED against documentation. The swechat n includes 50 Vertex ids that the loader stored as message ids (ids O1). The decoded server time agrees with client stamps in 155,067/155,267 = 0.99871 [0.99676, 0.99992] when every copy is counted; the full-data p50 offset is 3,781 ms [3,684, 3,871] (ids O2). One constant skew per stream brackets every id in all but 10 of 3,674 swechat streams, rate 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466], interval width p50 2,268 ms. A placebo that moves one response's first event 5 s earlier flags 1,441 streams, but moving it later flags 10, the baseline. The bracket therefore catches back-dating only, at per-turn resolution (ids O5, skeptic). aiv_cu Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini server ids show 0 violations against row inserts; OpenAI and Gemini ids have 1 s resolution (ids O3). The clocks that fail are client clocks: cc_local has 125 violations in 3 sessions, down to -7,749 ms (ids O6). Positive control: in the 2 re-stamped resume/fork session pairs, the request-id clock separates the copies (disagreeing offsets at least 619,473 ms vs agreeing 2,347-21,734 ms). The skeptic notes the re-stamp is also visible without the id clock, and n is 2 pairs (ids O7). In aiv_cu, Gemini's server-timing duration fits inside the logger's row gap with 0/12292 violations (min slack 563.8 ms), and rows never precede the HTTP Date (min 78.2 ms) (two_clocks O7). The Date header has 1 s resolution (D19). Harness timers already sit inside the client window: Glob 1/2090, Task 0/1023, Agent 0/1886 (two_clocks O8), and the bash_progress floor rule holds in 0/112677 events (two_clocks O9). Not yet measured: any client timer against the server interval between two request ids.
proposals.test_measurement: Data: raw swechat Claude Code transcripts (fix tolerances on split A, test on B) and cc_local; aiv_cu Gemini rows for the header variant. (1) Decode t_req for every assistant entry's requestId with the O1 decoder, and drop duplicate copies of shared ids (O7). (2) For each main-thread stream (session x agent), order requests by t_req. For each tool_use in response k whose tool_result is sent with request k+1, compute S = t_req(k+1) - t_req(k). Both ends are server times, so client skew cancels. Exclude run_in_background, Workflow and async Agent launches. (3) Compare S with every client-side duration claim for that round: the call->result timestamp gap; bash_progress max elapsedTimeSeconds; Glob/WebFetch/WebSearch durationMs; Task/Agent totalDurationMs; mcp_progress elapsedTimeMs. Flag D > S + tol, with tol fixed on split A before looking at B. Report the violation rate per timer type with session-clustered CIs, and the honest slack distribution (S - D)/S, which sets the smallest detectable overclaim factor. (4) Power: on B, inflate one call's durations by x2/x5/x10 and by +5/+30/+300 s (the O5 placebo design) and report flag rates. (5) Gemini variant in aiv_cu: S_g = (HTTP Date(k+1) - server-timing dur(k+1)) - HTTP Date(k), at 1 s resolution. This is the only per-round timing aiv_cu has, so test it against durations printed in shell results.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: re-stamped resume/fork copies, which give 190 offsets above 10 min when every copy is counted (ids O2) in 2 session pairs (ids O7); dedupe them before testing. Background or async launches whose result returns before the work ends: in cc_local the parent result precedes the last nested event in 63/63 Workflow/Agent calls, and 7/7 Agent calls had run_in_background=true (two_clocks O15); exclude these. 1 s resolution of OpenAI/Gemini ids and of the HTTP Date (ids O3, D19); tolerance must exceed it. Absorbed rather than false-alarming: client clock skew (ids O6) and machine suspend. In the one timer-over-timeout case, elapsed was 901 s against a 300000 ms timeout (two_clocks O10). Both interval ends are server times, and a suspended client sends its next request late. Unmeasured: clock skew between the provider servers minting consecutive ids; retry attempts; concurrent subagent streams (use only the parent stream's consecutive requests).
proposals.evasion_cost: Live fabrication (a lying tool backend, with the forger also writing the log): to make a round claim D seconds of work, the forger must hold the next API request for at least D, because the provider stamps receipt. Time can be padded but not compressed, so the cost is real wall-clock per fabricated call. Post-hoc retiming or inserting a round requires the forger to re-mint every affected request id: base58 UUIDv7 behind 'req_01', version 7, variant 2, chosen ms, plausible random bits. Each id must sit inside its stream's skew bracket and keep its order. Message ids must follow the format epoch (UUIDv7 only after 2026-07-06, ids O4). This is cheap for anyone who knows the layout; the ids note says these ids are unsigned. Re-minting becomes infeasible only if the verifier can look request ids up in the provider's own records, which was not tested here (UNVERIFIED). The model never sees request ids, Date or server-timing headers in its context and cannot predict server receipt times.
proposals.coverage: Measured: every Anthropic request in swechat CC (154,815 ids, 3,674 streams) and cc_local (31,085 ids). aiv_cu Gemini rows with timing headers: 12292 rows in 347 of 2000 B sessions (two_clocks O7). aiv_cc has 0 request ids stored (ids O13), so coverage there is 0. In aiv_cu, call and result share one stamp (lat == 0 for 59,956/59,956 calls, correlations O4), so the server interval would be the only per-round timing. The share of tool calls whose issuing and carrying requests both have ids in one stream is unmeasured.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Reading timestamps out of UUIDv7 is standard. My guess is that using the interval between two provider-minted request ids as a skew-free ceiling on client-claimed tool durations is uncommon. It adds nothing at capture time, unlike Hearsay, ACE or Tracekit. Prior art on forensic use of server-side request timestamps needs checking.
proposals.rank_reason: This is the only observed clock minted outside the forger's control, and it is present on every Anthropic request. Live fakery must pay real time, but post-hoc fakery stays cheap until provider lookup exists.

proposals.name: Commit-time freeze points: the git-held usage tally and agent_changes, amplified by the prompt-cache chain
proposals.observation_summary: At commit time the Entire CLI writes a 5-integer usage tally per session into checkpoint metadata in git. The tally equals an exact (tolerance 0) recount of the stored transcript in 4794/4836 = 0.9913 [0.9883, 0.9936] Claude-format sessions: full 2772, prefix 1664, window 358, none 42. In the prefix class the snapshot was taken while the session continued: created_at precedes the last transcript timestamp in 1664/1664 prefix sessions vs 39/2772 full ones, with a median of 3 messages past the snapshot (T1). The declared offset explains window sessions 357/357 (T2). After the dataset join fix, 33/5701 = 0.0058 [0.0041, 0.0081] remain unmatched (T3). Skeptic correction (T1): the tally recounts the transcript's own usage fields, so its only independent content is that it is a commit-time snapshot. agent_changes in the same commits copies Edit/Write inputs; 84335/95892 = 0.879 [0.863, 0.895] entries match a call on the exact key (commit_witness O7). Checkpoints are replicated: 1825 of 11581 checkpoint_ids appear in more than one repo (T9), and 4023 agent_changes entries trace to a same-name repo under another owner (commit_witness O7). Usage cascades along the cache chain, cache_read(k+1) = cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k). The chain holds exactly in 0.975 / 0.982 / 0.999 of clean swechat / cc_local / aiv_cc pairs (TC1), and in 59747/59804 aiv_cc pairs, run-clustered 0.99905 (aiv_accounting O9). Edits that leave usage untouched are caught only when large. At FPR 1%, the insertion detectable at power 0.5/0.9 is 8913/10000 chars (D_abs) and 6310/7079 chars (D_asym) in swechat CC, and 2239/2512 (D_abs) and 1778/2512 (D_asym) in aiv_cc (TC2). Edits to results under 1k chars are never detected (TC16).
proposals.test_measurement: Data: swechat Claude-format sessions with a matched tally (T1 full, prefix and window classes), their raw transcripts, checkpoint_metadata_raw and commits.agent_changes. (a) Freeze coverage: per session, the share of tool results timestamped before the snapshot boundary (whole transcript, prefix end, or the declared window), with session-clustered CIs. (b) Cascade amplification: for each frozen result j, count m_j, the later responses in the same unbroken cache chain inside the frozen span. A usage-consistent edit of delta tokens shifts the tally's cache_read sum by delta*m_j and cache_creation by delta. Simulate delta = 1 and delta = the TC2 threshold on every frozen result, re-run the T1 matcher, and report the share that flips from matched to none. (c) The forger's other option, editing text but not usage: report the TC2 power curve restricted to frozen spans. (d) Change one character of a frozen Edit/Write input, re-run the commit_witness O7 exact-key trace, and report the flip rate. (e) Replicas: per checkpoint, the number of repos that hold it (T9). These are copies a forger would also have to rewrite.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured honest floor: 33/5701 sessions unmatched after the join fix (T3). The rate is highest in CLI 0.5.x, 15/1048 = 0.0143 [0.0087, 0.0235] (T4). With output_tokens excluded, the Claude residuals classify as prefix 7, full 1, none 6, consistent with mid-stream snapshots (T4). In the dataset table, multi-checkpoint rows mix snapshots (39 sessions, T3); use the session_logs values. 1010 agent_changes entries appear in no released transcript, and 6524 belong to another session of the same repo (commit_witness O7), so the trace needs the checkpoint's wider session window. Cache-chain breaks from images, compaction and idle gaps stop the amplification at the break (aiv_accounting O9).
proposals.evasion_cost: Live fabrication evades this completely. The model really consumed the fake output, the provider counted it, and Entire snapshots the forged log. Post-hoc editing of a frozen span leaves two options. (a) Leave usage untouched. The edit must then stay below the conservation threshold: 6310 (D_asym) to 8913 (D_abs) chars at power 0.5 in swechat CC, 1778-2239 in aiv_cc; anything under 1k chars is free (TC16). It also must not touch an Edit/Write input that agent_changes copied. (b) Rewrite usage consistently. Recounting tokens with the provider tokenizer is cheap, and so is adding the delta to cache_read on every later response. But the frozen tally then stops matching at tolerance 0. Hiding that means rewriting the checkpoint commits on the entire/checkpoints branch, which is a force-push on any remote, and every fork that already copied the checkpoint (T9). The forger may not control those forks. The model never sees usage fields or the checkpoint branch. The forger can recompute everything except replicas they do not control. The tamper window before a freeze is the edit-to-commit lag: median 0.266 h [0.232, 0.302], p90 13.3 h (commit_witness O13). Push time is not in the data.
proposals.coverage: Measured: 4836 Claude-format sessions with api>0 have a tally, and 4794 match (T1). token_usage.api_call_count is filled in 12975/13406 checkpoint rows (raw_census A6-O6). Sessions linked to at least one ok commit: 4085/5850 = 0.698 [0.686, 0.710] (commit_witness O1). The share of tool results inside a frozen span is unmeasured. Prefix sessions leave a median of 3 messages unfrozen (T1). Only the SWE-chat/Entire repos have this; cc_local, aiv_cc and aiv_cu have no commit-time ledger.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. In effect this is hash-chain sealing (Agent Flight Recorder, NovaFabric), supplied incidentally by git and an attribution tool installed for other reasons. Two parts might be new. First, the cache-chain amplification, where a usage-consistent 1-token edit shifts the frozen cache_read sum once per later response. Second, treating fork replicas as copies outside the forger's control. Probably close to prior art; check before claiming.
proposals.rank_reason: A tolerance-0 match against a snapshot held in replicated git turns rewriting usage from cheap arithmetic into a history rewrite. It only binds post-hoc tampering, and only in Entire-linked sessions.

proposals.name: Nested timer chain: durations printed in tool output must fit inside model-invisible harness timers, which must fit inside the provider interval of proposal 1
proposals.observation_summary: In honest swechat CC data, harness timers the model never sees are tight and violation-free. bash_progress elapsed obeys the floor rule in 0/112677 events (Wilson hi 3.41e-5, 687 sessions). Ticks advance by 1 s, the first tick lands at elapsed 3 (3211 calls) or 2 (2449), and the result follows the last tick in 5676/5676 (two_clocks O9). mcp_progress elapsed equals completed - started exactly in 1014/1147 and is never negative (two_clocks O2). Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch, Task and Agent timers sit inside the call->result window: Glob 1/2090, the others 0 (two_clocks O8). Timestamp latency agrees with harness duration at 0.985 [0.979, 0.989] (correlations O8). Codex writes a model-visible 'Wall time' header that never exceeds the call->output gap on exec_command (0 violations of 4408). It sits -139.24 to -49.65 ms from the exec duration, but that offset rests on 5 sessions, 1 of which supplies 1604/2420 rows. shell_command headers exceed the gap in 646/1817 cases by up to 49 ms, because they display 0.1 s rounding (two_clocks O6). Coverage limits: the progress stream exists in 1981/4925 swechat CC files and in 0 cc_local files (raw_census A6-O10), and harness durations exist for only 2.8% of CC calls (correlations O8). No lens measured durations printed inside tool output, such as test-runner summaries or `time`.
proposals.test_measurement: Data: swechat CC Bash results that have bash_progress (fix regexes and tolerance on split A, test on B), plus Codex exec outputs with both 'Wall time' and exec_command_end duration. Pre-register regexes for durations that tools print: pytest 'in X s', go test 'ok <pkg> Xs', cargo/jest/npm 'Finished in', 'Time:', 'Done in', and the shell `time` 'real' line. For each match, require D_print <= last-tick elapsed + 1 s and D_print <= the call->result gap, and require the gap <= S from proposal 1. Exclude re-read commands (cat/tail/head/grep of files) and background-task outputs. Report coverage (the share of shell results that print a duration), the honest violation rate with session-clustered CIs, and power against two simulated forgers. (i) A lying backend: keep the printed text, but give the call an instant-return timing profile drawn from honest calls that print no duration. (ii) A padded backend: sleep for D_print. This should pass, and it measures what the forger pays in wall-clock.
proposals.false_positive_source: Re-reads: in the commit-claim data, 15 of 19 out-of-window cases were cat/tail/head/grep re-reads of earlier output files such as background-task .output files (commit_witness O11). Durations printed inside re-read logs belong to earlier runs, so command class must exclude them. Display rounding: 646/1817 Codex shell_command headers exceed the gap by up to 49 ms (two_clocks O6), so the tolerance must exceed the printed precision. Machine suspend: 1 progress event exceeded its timeout among 83521 (elapsed 901 s vs 300000 ms), and elapsed advanced with wall time in 377 of 378 long tick gaps (two_clocks O10). Long tails do not violate a ceiling: 435 of the 611 top-1% shell latencies run past their own timeout (D10). Unmeasured: runners that report cached results or cumulative times.
proposals.evasion_cost: Against a lying tool backend behind an honest harness: to print 'N passed in 45 s', the backend must actually take 45 s, because the harness measures bash_progress ticks and the call->result gap. The cost is real wall-clock per fake, or printing implausibly short durations. A forger who also controls the harness must regenerate a consistent 1 Hz tick chain: floored elapsed, a per-call phase lock (residual range median 6 ms), a first tick at 2-3 s, and timeoutMs equal to the argument. They must also regenerate durationMs and the timestamps. That is cheap to compute, and after that only proposal 1's provider interval still binds. The model sees its tool output, and in Codex the Wall time header. It does not see bash_progress, durationMs or mcp elapsed.
proposals.coverage: Harness side, measured: 112677 bash_progress events over 5702 calls in 687 sessions (two_clocks O9). The progress stream exists in 1981/4925 swechat CC files and 0/332 cc_local main files (raw_census A6-O10). Harness durations exist on 2.8% of CC calls (correlations O8), and Codex exec outputs carry a Wall time header in 4408 cases (two_clocks O6). The share of tool outputs that print a duration is unmeasured. Current Claude Code (cc_local) falls back to the call->result gap alone.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. METR-style recomputation checks what a command prints. My guess is that checking the time a tool claims it took against independent timers at two trust levels is less common. Part of this is ordinary log-consistency checking.
proposals.rank_reason: Model-invisible harness timers are tight enough to bound a lying tool server. But a forger who controls the harness defeats them, current Claude Code no longer writes them, and the content side is unmeasured.

proposals.name: Prompt-cache state as a server-computed stopwatch and unchanged-prefix certificate
proposals.observation_summary: The provider reports how much of each request matched its prompt cache. The chain cache_read(k+1) = cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) holds in 59747/59804 aiv_cc clean pairs. Breaks track elapsed time: 49/59772 pairs break at gaps under 300 s, against 8/32 at 300 s or more. Image pairs hold in 4367/4570, compaction pairs in 0/933 (aiv_accounting O9). The exact chain holds in 0.975 / 0.982 / 0.999 of clean swechat / cc_local / aiv_cc pairs (TC1). Unlogged history edits surface as resets. In 30 non-compaction pairs across 12 aiv_cc runs, cache_read resets to 20401-21400 (the system prefix) with no compact_boundary row; 0/30 carry a context_management object, and 27/30 are image pairs (aiv_accounting O12). In swechat CC, the 616 clean pairs with a cache_read drop exceed the conservation threshold at 0.166 vs 0.009, and they are 47 of the 71 pairs with |r| > 20000 (TC12). Model switches force misses: 69/89 overall and 40/43 on a switch to Haiku, but only 15/31 on a return from Haiku (changepoints O9). A missing harness channel produces unexplained drops: aiv_cu SDK drops sit 5.9-13.4 s from compaction rows that only aiv_cc logs (changepoints O8). aiv_cc has no decodable server id (ids O13), so cache state is its only server-side time signal.
proposals.test_measurement: (a) TTL curve: in swechat CC, estimate P(cache-chain break) as a function of the skew-free server interval S from proposal 1, per model; in aiv_cc, as a function of the created_at gap. Pre-register the gap bins on split A. (b) Retiming test on split B: shift a random round's client timestamps by +/-k minutes while keeping usage, and report how often the (gap bin, break/hit) pair becomes implausible under the split-A curve. (c) Unchanged-prefix certificate: flag pairs where cache_read(k+1) < cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) and no logged compaction, image, model switch or above-TTL gap is present. Report per-corpus counts against the honest aiv_cc count of 30 (aiv_accounting O12), and join across tables before flagging (changepoints O8).
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured: idle gaps of 300 s or more break only 8/32 pairs, so a cache hit after a long claimed gap is not evidence (aiv_accounting O9). Image pairs hold only 4367/4570, and compaction pairs 0/933 (aiv_accounting O9). Client-side pruning leaves no log marker (30 resets, aiv_accounting O12). Model switches miss 69/89, and returns to a recent model often hit (only 15/31 miss) (changepoints O9). Some compactions are logged only in another table (changepoints O8). Unmeasured: cache TTL tiers and refresh-on-hit rules, and proxies that do not pass cache fields through.
proposals.evasion_cost: A post-hoc forger who retimes a round but leaves usage alone creates either a break at a short gap or a hit pattern at odds with the claimed gap. Only the first is informative (base rate 49/59772). Compressing a real long gap is therefore caught only when the provider actually expired the cache, which happened in 8/32 long gaps in aiv_cc. A forger who rewrites usage needs only arithmetic and a guess at the TTL rules. A guess of 'hit' is safe because long-gap hits are common. A live forger who silently rewrites earlier history before sending a request (for example, to hide a failed tool result from the model) gets a provider-computed cache_read that resets to the edit point. They must also rewrite the logged usage. That is cheap unless usage is frozen (proposal 2) or reconciled against provider billing, which is not in the data. The model never sees cache fields.
proposals.coverage: Every consecutive response pair with usage: 59804 clean aiv_cc pairs in 190 runs of one agent (aiv_accounting O9). TC1's pipeline has 154189 swechat CC pairs, 30210 cc_local pairs and 35307 aiv_cc pairs. Providers that report no cache fields are not covered.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED. Prompt-cache hits are known as a timing side channel in security work. I have not seen anyone read the provider's reported cache_read as a certificate of how much history was unchanged, or as a coarse server-side stopwatch for logs that carry no server ids. Low confidence.
proposals.rank_reason: Server-computed, invisible to the model, and the only server-side timing in aiv_cc. But long gaps seldom force a miss (8/32), and the cache arithmetic is cheap for a forger to recompute.

proposals.name: Provider quantization lattices in usage fields as a trap for synthesized rounds
proposals.observation_summary: Provider-computed usage numbers sit on undocumented lattices. Codex cached_input_tokens is a multiple of 128 in 16106/16106 calls. So are OpenCode per-message cache reads for GPT/OpenAI-family models (11393/11393), but only 1/563 for Claude models (T11). Gemini IMAGE prompt tokens move by 0 or exactly one per-model unit in 11668/11668 pairs. They increase in 5059/5092 GUI windows and in 0 shell (0/4134) or get_pixel_coords (0/2033) windows (TC9). The unit is set by model generation: 258 for gemini-2.5-pro, 1064 for 3.x, and a third constant, 2160, in 3 sessions; no session mixes lattices (0/309) (D3). Uncached input collapses onto a per-model constant: opus-4-6 takes value 1 in 0.835 of responses, and aiv_cc shows 8 x30427 and 10 x5024 (D7). Codex reasoning tokens pile onto 516 + 518k, with no known mechanism; 140/6910 rows are on the lattice (D1).

checks.name: 1. Provider-clock ceiling on each tool round (interval between consecutive server-minted request ids bounds client duration claims)
checks.overclaims:
All 15 cited observations are in _index.json with reproduced == true. The quoted figures match the skeptic's numbers: 154,815/154,815 including the 50 Vertex ids; 155,067/155,267 = 0.99871; p50 3,781 [3,684, 3,871]; 10/3,674 streams, 0.00272; placebo 1,441 vs 10; 0/12292 with min 563.8 ms; Glob 1/2090; 0/112677; 63/63 and 7/7. The skeptic corrections for O5 (one-sided, per-turn), O7 (n = 2 pairs, re-stamp visible without the id clock) and D19 (1 s resolution) are applied.

Problems:
(a) The core comparison, a client timer against S = t_req(k+1) - t_req(k), has never been run. Honest slack and power are unknown. S includes all of response k's generation time, so its tightness is unknown. The proposal does say this.
(b) The evasion argument contradicts itself. 'Live fakery must pay real time' holds only if the forger leaves request ids alone. The stated live threat model has the forger also writing the log, and the proposal itself says re-minting unsigned ids is cheap. Against an informed log-writing forger, the ceiling binds only if ids can be looked up with the provider, which is untested. Against a lying backend behind an honest harness, the harness timers and the call->result gap (proposal 3) already bind. So the extra value of this proposal is limited to forgers who rewrite timestamps but not ids.
(c) The rank reason calls this 'the only observed clock minted outside the forger's control'. That is wrong. Anthropic msg UUIDv7 after 2026-07-06 (ids O4), OpenAI and Gemini ids (ids O3) and the Gemini Date/server-timing headers (two_clocks O7) are also provider-minted. All of them reach the verifier only as client-logged copies. For the same reason, the coverage claim that the Gemini header is 'the only per-round timing aiv_cu has' ignores the O3 server ids.
(d) 'Client clock skew is absorbed' is true only for constant skew. D is a client-clock difference, and ids O6 skeptic measured within-session drift above 2 s in 15 swechat sessions (none above 10 s) and in 2 of 18 cc_local sessions. A clock step during a call inflates D, so the tolerance must cover the measured drift.
(e) The FP section attributes the '190 offsets above 10 min' to the 2 re-stamped pairs. Only 178 come from those pairs (ids O7). 12 far offsets remain after dedupe (ids O2) and have no explanation.
(f) The 'present on every Anthropic request' claim fails for aiv_cc, which stores 0 request ids (ids O13); the coverage section admits this. ids O3 is weak by construction (row insert lags by a median of 5.7-12 s), and 'the clocks that fail are client clocks' rests on 1-2 sessions (ids O6 skeptic).
(g) 'The model never sees request ids' is reasoning, not an observation.
checks.prior_art_overlap_with_listed: No direct overlap with the listed items. It adds nothing at capture time, unlike Hearsay, ACE, Tracekit and Tool Receipts (HMAC runtime receipts are the nearest neighbour). It is not hash-chain sealing. It differs from the recomputation, jc and shadow-state approaches. Prior art on forensic use of server-side request timestamps is unchecked, so novelty stays UNVERIFIED.

(b) The 'cascade amplification' is redundant against a tolerance-0 tally. proposals.name: Server-minted request-id bracket as a stretch guard for latency checks
proposals.observation_summary: Anthropic request ids are UUIDv7 rendered in base58: 154,815/154,815 v7|var2 in swechat (this count includes 50 Vertex ids the loader stored as api_msg_id) and 31,085/31,085 in cc_local. The layout was inferred from data and is UNVERIFIED against vendor documentation (ids/O1). Their server time agrees with the client stamps: swechat non-Vertex n=155,267 (session, request) pairs in 1,638 sessions, 10 violations all in 1 session, agreement 0.99871 [0.99676, 0.99992] counting every copy, full-data p50 offset 3,781 ms [3,684, 3,871]; holdout A has 11,047 ids with 0 violations (ids/O2, skeptic numbers). One constant skew per stream places every id between the last input event and the first output block: swechat 10 of 3,674 streams inconsistent, rate 0.00272 [0.00112, 0.00466], slack U-L p5 1,102 / p50 2,268 / p95 3,807 ms; cc_local 1 of 847 streams, even though client skew produces 125 naive-rule violations in 3 sessions (ids/O5, ids/O6). Placebo on 3,673 swechat streams: moving one response's first event 5 s earlier flags 1,441 and 30 s earlier flags 3,581, while moving it 5/30/300 s later flags 10, the baseline. Power is therefore one-sided and per turn (ids/O5 skeptic). The id clock picked the original over the re-stamped copy in 178/178 resume/fork splits (ids/O7). aiv_cu server-minted ids (Anthropic msg after 2026-07-06, OpenAI items, Gemini responseId) show 0 violations (ids/O3). aiv_cc stores no request ids (ids/O13).
proposals.test_measurement: Phase B Probe 1 flags results that arrive faster than the work allows. A post-hoc forger's cheapest evasion is to move the result stamp later, or to shift the rest of the stream. Test whether the bracket closes that route, reusing the ids lens bracket code on swechat CC (B and holdout A) and cc_local: (a) delay one randomly chosen tool result by D in {1, 2, 5, 30, 300} s, keeping file order and leaving every request id untouched; recompute L = max(last input ts - id time) and U = min(first block ts - id time) per stream, and count flagged streams; (b) a consistent re-stamp variant that shifts that result and every later client event by D; (c) the same per turn on aiv_cu, using created_at against the decoded Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini ids. Report flags per D against the honest 10/3,674 (swechat) and 1/847 (cc_local) with session-clustered CIs. Also report the share of Probe-1-flagged fast results whose stream slack would let a forger stretch them up to the honest floor without tripping the bracket. Delaying an input is the mirror of the measured output-advance placebo (both shrink U - L), but it has not been run, so its power is UNVERIFIED.
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured honest flags: 10/3,674 swechat streams (10 sessions) and 1/847 cc_local. The count depends on tolerance: 0 s gives 18, 5 s gives 7 (ids/O5). Known sources: re-stamped resume/fork copies, where copied history was collapsed onto 1-2 timestamps (477 entries in 2 session pairs; ids/O7); bulk-stamped history in old Claude Code (call->result gap exactly 0 in 498/137,380 main-thread pairs, 177 sessions; two_clocks/O12); client clock skew or steps within a stream (cc_local, ids/O6; the per-stream skew absorbs a constant offset but not a step); Vertex ids stored in the message-id column (50, ids/O1). Wide-slack streams (U - L p95 3,807 ms) give coarser resolution.
proposals.evasion_cost: Delaying a result past the stream slack requires rewriting the server-minted id of the next request, and of every later request if the rest of the stream is shifted. The forger must decode and re-encode base58 UUIDv7 under a layout we only inferred, keeping the version/variant bits and one consistent skew per stream. The agent cannot influence when the provider mints the id. Whether request ids ever enter the model's context was not measured (UNVERIFIED; they are harness fields of the transcript). Not caught: making a result earlier (the later-shift placebo equals the baseline), and an execution-path compromise with honest stamps, where the bracket adds nothing beyond Probe 1 itself. Resolution is per turn, on the order of the stream slack (p50 2,268 ms).
proposals.coverage: swechat Claude Code: 155,267 (session, request) pairs in 1,638 sessions (ids/O2), against 1,679 Claude Code transcript files in split B (two_clocks/O1); the bracket was evaluated on 3,674 streams. cc_local: 31,085/31,085 request ids decodable, 847 streams. aiv_cu: per turn only, since every call has lat == 0 (59,956/59,956; correlations/O4). Anthropic msg ids carry time only from 2026-07-06 (0 v7 from 2025-04 to 2026-06; ids/O4); OpenAI items 14,038 ids; Gemini responseIds 12,292 (1 s resolution). Bracket streams: 105/80/27/32 Anthropic, 255/92 Gemini, 463 OpenAI. Not covered: aiv_cc (0 request ids; 35,452 msg ids decode at chance level, ids/O13); Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI (only client-minted id clocks from the same process as the stamps); Who&When (no clock). Two of five scaffold families.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: decoding provider-minted UUIDv7 request ids as a third clock that bounds client-side agent log stamps looks uncommon in agent-log work. UUIDv7 time extraction and skew bracketing are standard distributed-systems forensics, and the bracket itself is the ids lens's candidate. The possibly new part is using it specifically to close the stretch evasion of our latency-physics check.
proposals.rank_reason: Largest measured share of tool calls bound by a clock the agent does not control, with a measured honest stream rate of 0.00272 and measured per-turn power, in two of five families.

proposals.name: Usage-ledger propagation check: parameter-free usage identities over every API turn, anchored by out-of-band tallies
proposals.observation_summary: Provider usage obeys exact, parameter-free identities in every scaffold family we hold. The cache-append chain cache_read(k+1) = cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) holds in 0.975 / 0.982 / 0.999 of clean pairs (swechat CC / cc_local / aiv_cc; TC1 skeptic) and in 59,747/59,804 aiv_cc pairs (aiv_accounting/O9). Codex cached input is a multiple of 128 in 16,106/16,106 calls, and OpenCode GPT-family cache.read in 11,393/11,393 (T11). The Codex cumulative chain holds 15,302/15,386 once duplicate events are dropped, and 81/84 remaining breaks follow a compaction or rollback (A6-O7 skeptic). OpenCode total = in + out + cache.read + cache.write in 14,639/14,854 (post hoc; A6-O8). Gemini CLI total = in + out + thoughts in 5,141/5,141 (A6-O9). Gemini prompt IMAGE tokens move by 0 or one per-model unit in 11,668/11,668 pairs (TC9) and sit on {258, 1064, 2160} in 10,569/10,569 pro rows (D3). aiv_cc result ledger: num_turns = user rows + 1 in 153/154 non-trivial runs, and cost is linear in tokens in 193/193 (aiv_accounting/O4, O5). In swechat, a commit-time tally written by the Entire CLI equals a recount of the transcript in 4,794/4,836 Claude-format sessions, with 33/5,701 unmatched across 4 scaffolds after the join fix (T1, T3). The conservation residual exists for 8 units (TC1 pairs: swechat CC 154,189; cc_local 30,210; aiv_cc 35,307; Codex 6,842; OpenCode 5,334; Gemini CLI 1,896; aiv_cu Anthropic 22,673; aiv_cu Gemini 11,945), but its content power is weak. At realized FPR 0.0101, an inserted change needs 8,913 / 10,000 chars for power 0.5 / 0.9 in swechat CC (aiv_cc 2,239 / 2,512), and deleting a result under 1k chars is never detected (TC2, TC16 skeptic).
proposals.test_measurement: Per unit, list which identities apply and their honest hold rates (above). Run a tamper simulation on honest split-B sessions: (1) delete one tool-result turn, (2) duplicate a turn, (3) swap two adjacent turns, (4) add or remove k chars in one result without touching usage, (5) an informed forger who recomputes every later usage field arithmetically (cache propagation, 128-multiples, image units, cumulative totals). For each, count sessions flagged by any exact identity, by the conservation residual (thresholds from the other fold, as in TC2), and by the commit-time tally (swechat only). Report per unit the share of API turns covered by at least one exact identity, and the share of tool results large enough for conservation power >= 0.5. In swechat CC only the [10000,100000) bin (n 8,788) reaches 0.973 for whole-result deletion, against 0.085 for [1000,10000) (n 40,056), 0.003 for [100,1000) (n 61,269) and 0.009 for [0,100) (n 30,914) (TC16).
proposals.false_positive_source: Measured honest breaks of the cache chain in aiv_cc: idle gaps of 300 s or more (8/32 break, against 49/59,772 below 300 s), image pairs (4,367/4,570 hold) and every compaction pair (0/933 hold) (aiv_accounting/O9); 30 non-compaction context resets with no compact_boundary row (aiv_accounting/O12). The Codex chain breaks at compaction/rollback (81/84). The OpenCode identity is post hoc. Tally residual: 33/5,701 sessions over 18 repos (T3, T4). Conservation tail: hidden-content tools (ToolSearch residual median +897.4 with 0 logged chars, TC4; ExitPlanMode median -1,357.4, TC13).
proposals.evasion_cost: Under an execution-path compromise with an honest harness, the model really received the fake output, so usage conserves and nothing breaks. This family only addresses after-the-fact edits. Against those, every identity is arithmetic that a forger holding the transcript can recompute and propagate through all later turns, and conservation is evaded by any change below 8,913 chars (swechat CC, power 0.5) or by length-preserving substitution. What the forger cannot get from the transcript alone is the provider tokenizer (conservation residual medians of tens of tokens in coding scaffolds, TC1) and, in swechat, the commit-time tally held in a git branch outside the transcript (T1). The agent does not see its own usage numbers in context (UNVERIFIED).
proposals.coverage: The only witness measured in all five scaffold families: conservation pairs for 8 units (TC1), and at least one exact identity measured for Claude Code formats (cache chain), Codex (128-granularity, cumulative chain), OpenCode (total identity; 128-granularity on GPT-family models), Gemini CLI (total identity) and AI Village (aiv_cc cache chain and result ledger; aiv_cu Gemini image units). TC1 reports no aiv_cu OpenAI/compat unit and nothing for Who&When. Effective content coverage is small: only results of several thousand chars and up are constrained (TC2, TC16). The out-of-band tally exists only in swechat.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: this builds on our own Phase A token-conservation plan and on the aiv_accounting, swechat_tables and distributions lens candidates (cache-chain continuity, provider lattices, out-of-band ledger). The possibly new part is requiring all identities jointly, so that one inserted or deleted turn must be propagated through every later usage record and an external tally. LLM billing-reconciliation tooling may already do similar bookkeeping.
proposals.rank_reason: Broadest scaffold coverage of any measured witness (all five families, every API turn), but it constrains turn structure far better than result content, and its identities are recomputable.

Version drift: cc_local subagent files carry no Read numLines (0/12), and Glob totalMatches is 0/6,422 in swechat against 1,231/1,234 in cc_local (A6-O1, A6-O4). Codex shell_command headers at 0.1 s display resolution exceed the gap in 646/1,817 by at most 49 ms (two_clocks/O6). The IR drops tool_reference blocks (TC4).
proposals.evasion_cost: Catches only a forger who edits the visible text and not the structured record. Line counts and nested-call counts are trivially recomputable by anyone holding the transcript. structuredPatch line positions and Read totalLines depend on the real file, which is costlier to fake consistently across calls. The structured record is a transcript field that the model does not receive (UNVERIFIED), so the agent cannot tune it in flight. Under an execution-path compromise with an honest harness, both renderings derive from the same fake output, so a faked Bash result gives no signal here.
proposals.coverage: Claude Code formats dominate swechat (format counts: claude_code 4,925, opencode 623, codex 213, gemini 59, cursor 23; A6-O16). Within them, Read, Edit and Grep results carry a field at 0.972 / 0.960 / 0.863. Harness duration fields exist for only 2.8% of CC calls (correlations/O8). Codex has an exec duration on every exec event (13,876/13,876 in 67 files), but the Wall-time identity was measured on only 5 sessions, one of which supplies 1,604/2,420. OpenCode has bash state.time.end on 5,311/5,317 (A6-O3); its other metadata were not measured. AI Village: only aiv_cc tool durations (WebFetch 29, Glob 133, WebSearch 47 results; aiv_accounting/O3). aiv_cu, Gemini CLI and Who&When are not covered. Three of five families, CC-heavy.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: the neighbours are recomputation (METR) and output-grammar parsing (jc). This compares two harness renderings of one result instead of recomputing from inputs. It generalises the raw_census lens's structured-counter recount across scaffolds. Harness developers likely know the redundancy; we have not seen it used for fabrication detection.
proposals.rank_reason: Exact identities with whitelisted honest FP over the largest call counts in the dominant coding format, across three families, but trivially recomputable and blind to execution-path compromise.

proposals.name: Provider-clock action windows for logs without per-call stamps (AI Village computer use)
proposals.observation_summary: aiv_cu is the largest corpus (78,114 sessions; D2, changepoints/O4) and has no per-call latency: every call has lat == 0 (59,956/59,956; correlations/O4). Each turn still carries clocks the agent does not write: Google's HTTP Date and server-timing on Gemini rows, and provider-minted ids for all three providers. On Gemini rows the server duration always fits inside the DB row gap (0/12,292, Wilson hi 3.12e-4, 347 sessions; slack min 563.8 ms, median 6,079), and created_at never precedes the HTTP Date (min 78.2 ms; two_clocks/O7). The Date precedes the row insert in 3,246/3,246 flash and 8,990/8,990 pro call rows, with medians -4,434 / -4,574 ms; the order is unambiguous at 1 s resolution in 2,831/3,246 and 7,276/8,990 (D19 skeptic). Because the row is inserted after the action runs, created_at minus the Date bounds action execution plus client overhead. Provider id times also precede the row with 0 violations: Anthropic opus 3,481 ids (min 1,297 ms, p50 11,607), OpenAI 14,038 (min 450, hex50 p50 5,716), Gemini 12,292 (ids/O3). For those ids the window also contains generation. Gemini server timing tracks reasoning (srv_ms vs resp_think 0.517 [0.477, 0.562]; correlations/O7).
proposals.test_measurement: On aiv_cu split B, then the population, compute per Gemini row w = created_at - HTTP Date. Per OpenAI/Anthropic row, compute w' = created_at - decoded id time minus a generation allowance fitted on split A from output tokens. Stratify by action (shell, gui, get_pixel_coords, pause) and by shell command class. Positive controls: pause actions and shell commands with an explicit sleep or timeout must satisfy w >= requested duration - 1 s; report the honest violation rate with session-clustered CIs. Then measure separability: compare w for commands whose output reports multi-second work (installs, builds, test runs, pushes) against trivial commands, with a threshold pre-registered on split A, and report the rate at which honest long-work outputs fall under it.
proposals.false_positive_source: 1 s HTTP Date resolution: 415 flash and 1,714 pro rows lie within 1 s of the insert, so their order is ambiguous (D19). Client overhead: gap - dur is at least 563.8 ms (two_clocks/O7). Screenshot capture and row-write time on GUI actions. For Anthropic/OpenAI rows, generation inside the window (opus id-to-row p50 11,607 ms) loosens the bound. Occasional late writes: 17 rows with updated_at more than 1 s after created_at (D6). No Anthropic msg-id clock before 2026-07-06 (ids/O4).
proposals.evasion_cost: Under an execution-path compromise the fake action finishes fast, so a claim of long work inside a short provider-bounded window is caught. The forger's cheap evasion is to pad the fake with a sleep, the same weakness any latency check has. After the fact, a forger would have to rewrite AI Village's DB created_at and the stored provider headers and ids consistently. The agent sees neither at action time (UNVERIFIED that the headers never reach the model).
proposals.coverage: Tight bounds only on Gemini rows: 12,292 rows in 347 of 2,000 aiv_cu B sessions (two_clocks/O7). Looser, generation-inclusive bounds on OpenAI items (14,038 ids) and on Anthropic msg ids after 2026-07-06 (0 v7 from 2025-04 to 2026-06; ids/O4). Other corpora already have per-call stamps for Probe 1, so this adds coverage only to AI Village computer use, one family.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: using LLM-provider HTTP Date and server-timing headers as an execution-time bound for agent actions looks uncommon. HTTP Date headers are a known web-forensics artefact, and the ordering check is the two_clocks lens's third-party bracketing candidate. The possibly new part is turning it into an action-duration witness where the harness has none.
proposals.rank_reason: Adds a timing witness to the largest corpus, where per-call latency does not exist, but tight bounds cover only Gemini rows in one family.

proposals.name: Image-token quanta as a screenshot-count witness for GUI agents
proposals.observation_summary: In GUI sessions the text log holds almost nothing to check: aiv_cu GUI results carry text in 0.0002 of rows, and STOP-narration string support falls from 0.657 (no GUI) to 0.286 (GUI share above half) (N5 skeptic). Provider usage still records what reached the model. Gemini prompt IMAGE tokens change by 0 or exactly one per-model unit in 11,668/11,668 pairs (258 for gemini-2.5-pro; 1064 for 3.x). The increment is positive in 5,059/5,092 GUI windows and 0 in all shell (0/4,134), get_pixel_coords (0/2,033) and pause (0/202) windows (TC9 skeptic), and prompt IMAGE counts sit on {258, 1064, 2160} in 10,569/10,569 pro rows (D3). In the Anthropic Agent SDK stream the residual per stripped image is tightly concentrated: median 890.1 (887.9-890.9), p25 879.1, p75 892.7 over 4,543 image pairs (aiv_accounting/O11 skeptic); single-image windows give 1,035.0, p5-p95 1,016-1,142 (TC17). Where image sizes vary the quantum is lost (swechat CC 535.0, p5-p95 121-1,618; TC17).
proposals.test_measurement: For aiv_cu Gemini, compare the image count implied by dIMAGE / unit in each window with the number of screenshot-returning actions logged there. Report honest agreement (5,059/5,092 positive GUI windows; inspect the 33 without an increment) and the detection rate when one GUI action is inserted into or deleted from honest windows. Refit aiv_cu Anthropic conservation with an image term (TC1 left it out: GUI windows have residual median +206.5 against -602.8 for shell) to see whether a per-image quantum appears, as in aiv_cc. Then cross with narration: compare the rate of narrated on-screen facts (titles, counts, URLs) in windows or sessions with zero image increment against GUI windows.
proposals.false_positive_source: 33/5,092 honest GUI windows with no increment, unexplained (TC9). Pruning beyond 40 images is untested, while 442 population Gemini sessions exceed 40 GUI turns (TC9). Units are model-specific, and gemini-3.8-flash (277 pairs) never shows an image (TC9). In Anthropic streams images share the residual with text framing, and unlogged context resets hit image pairs (27 of 30; aiv_accounting/O12). Image sizes vary where users paste images (TC17).
proposals.evasion_cost: A forger who inserts or deletes GUI actions after the fact must also edit promptTokensDetails (Gemini) or the usage/cache chain (Anthropic) by exact unit multiples in every later turn. That is recomputable arithmetic once the unit is known. The check witnesses only that an image of the expected size reached the model, not what the image showed. The agent does not see its usage breakdown (UNVERIFIED).
proposals.coverage: aiv_cu Gemini: 11,945 conservation pairs with 5,092 GUI windows in split B (TC1, TC9). aiv_cc: 4,543 image pairs in 64 runs of one agent (aiv_accounting/O11). GUI-heavy sessions are a large part of AI Village: 983 of the 2,192 sampled sessions have a GUI share above half (N5, N2). Not covered: aiv_cu Anthropic and OpenAI until an image term is fitted, coding scaffolds (images are rare and variable), Who&When. One family.
proposals.novelty_guess_unverified: UNVERIFIED: per-image token quanta as a screenshot-count witness for GUI agents look uncommon. This extends the token_conservation lens's Gemini IMAGE ledger to Anthropic residual quanta and to narration grounding.
proposals.rank_reason: Fills the GUI gap where text-based checks fail, but is tight only for Gemini rows and one aiv_cc agent.

checks.overclaims: All 11 citations are in _index.json with reproduced == true. Every quoted number matches the skeptic's figures. (2) The rank_reason cites 'measured per-turn power', but the measured placebo shifts a response's first event earlier (output back-dating). The skeptic says 'later copy' follows from the offsets, calling the agreeing copy 'original' is an inference, and the collapse onto 1-2 timestamps is detectable without any id clock. checks.name: Usage-ledger propagation check: parameter-free usage identities over every API turn, anchored by out-of-band tallies
checks.overclaims: All 18 citations are reproduced, and the numbers match the skeptic's figures. Overclaims: (1) The title says 'anchored by out-of-band tallies'. The skeptic (T1 and the swechat_tables overclaim) says the Entire tally is a deterministic recount of the transcript's own usage fields. Its only independent content is a commit-time snapshot, and it says nothing about whether a tool result is real. It also exists only in swechat and holds just 5 integers per session. Of the 4,794 matches, 1,664 are prefix and 358 are window matches, so it constrains the transcript only up to the snapshot. 'Out-of-band' should become 'commit-time snapshot, swechat only'. (2) The title and rank_reason claim 'every API turn', but the share of turns covered by any exact identity is unmeasured; the proposal's own test lists it as to-do. The cache chain excludes compaction pairs (0/933) and some image pairs, and aiv_cu Anthropic and OpenAI have no exact identity measured. (3) The swechat CC cache chain holds in only 0.975 of clean pairs (cc_local 0.982), across 154,189 pairs in about 1,641 sessions. Honest breaks would therefore be routine at session level, yet the false-positive section lists only aiv_cc break causes, and the swechat CC and cc_local breaks are uncharacterised. The planned 'sessions flagged by any exact identity' metric will be dominated by them. (4) The aiv_cu Anthropic (22,673) and Gemini (11,945) units are counted as conservation witnesses. The TC1/TC2 skeptic says aiv_cu residuals mix in screenshots that never appear in the IR (GUI windows +206.5, shell -602.8), so they are not conservation noise. (5) The aiv_cc power figures (2,239 / 2,512) come from one agent in one SDK session, and the TC2 skeptic warns they overstate generality. (6) 'Tens of tokens' leaves out cc_local's p50 of 152.2. (7) The aiv_accounting O9 skeptic notes the identities cover only server usage fields, not logged content. The proposal concedes this ('turn structure').
checks.prior_art_overlap_with_listed: Partial. Joint propagation through every later record is the same idea as listed hash-chain sealing (Agent Flight Recorder, NovaFabric), except the chain here occurs naturally and anyone can recompute it. The commit-time Entire tally is in effect a capture-side record already present, close to the listed capture-side witnesses. Each identity also repackages existing lens candidates: cache-chain continuity, log-vs-ledger, 128-granularity, cumulative counter chain, and our own Phase A conservation plan. The 'jointly' novelty claim is weak, because each identity is arithmetic a forger propagates anyway.

checks.name: Provider-clock action windows for logs without per-call stamps (AI Village computer use)
checks.overclaims: All 9 citations are reproduced, and the numbers match the skeptic's figures (563.8 ms, not the lens's wrong 0.45 s; D19 call-row counts and its 1 s ambiguity). Overclaims: (1) The summary says each turn carries agent-independent clocks, with 'provider-minted ids for all three providers'. Internally it is the two_clocks 'third-party clock bracketing' candidate fused with Phase B Probe 1 latency physics, as the proposal acknowledges. The same UNVERIFIED pointer as for proposal 1 applies: event-time bounding from causally ordered external clocks is classic digital forensics (Gladyshev & Patel line), and HTTP Date as a forensic artefact is known.
